label: prf:crystal-isospin-degeneracy
title: Proof of crystal isospin degeneracy
html:
Proof. The crystal-limit character \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\sigma) on a single Hecke generator \sigma is, by crystal-graph realisation, the trace of the signed-permutation action

  \sigma_i : T \;\longmapsto\; \mathrm{sign}(\rho_T(i)) \cdot T,
  \qquad \rho_T(i) := c(T(i+1)) - c(T(i))

on the standard-Young-tableaux basis \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda), where c(\cdot) is the cell content (content scaling). The Hecke involutivity at q = 0 — equivalently, reading off the relation \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i on the crystal sub-quotient from the Hecke skein convention (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 specialised at q = 0 — gives

  \sigma_i^{-1} : T \;\longmapsto\; \mathrm{sign}(\rho_T(i)) \cdot T
  \;=\; \sigma_i \cdot T

acting on the same SYT eigenline. The crystal-limit generators therefore act diagonally on the SYT basis with eigenvalues that are individually invariant under \sigma_i \leftrightarrow \sigma_i^{-1}. For any fixed T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda), the eigenvalue product along a braid word

  \mu^\lambda_T(\beta) \;:=\; \prod_{\ell \,\in\, \beta} \mathrm{eigval}_T(\ell)

is therefore equal under \beta \to \beta'. Note that \mu^\lambda_T is not the character \chi^\lambda — it is the eigenvalue product on the line through T; the character is the trace

  \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta) \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)}
      \mu^\lambda_T(\beta).

The trace is not multiplicative in \beta, but it is a sum of sign-flip-invariant per-eigenline contributions, so

  \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta_A)
    \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} \mu^\lambda_T(\beta_A)
    \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} \mu^\lambda_T(\beta_A')
    \;=\; \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta_A')

per partition. Summing against the (sign-independent) Plancherel weight w_\lambda(q = 1) = (f^\lambda)^2 / (3A)! yields the claim. \square

Conditional corollary (legacy disjoint-product convention). Suppose tritium and helium-3 are presented by the simplified disjoint-product words used by the canonical formalism

  \tilde\beta_T = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_4\sigma_5^{-1}\sigma_4
              \sigma_7\sigma_8^{-1}\sigma_7,
  \qquad
  \tilde\beta_{{}^3\mathrm{He}} = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_4\sigma_5\sigma_4^{-1}
              \sigma_7\sigma_8^{-1}\sigma_7

(differing only at positions 5 and 6 by paired inversion). Then

  S_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\tilde\beta_T) \;=\; S_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\tilde\beta_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}),

matching the witness term7-alpha5-crystal-derivation.witness.json which records both values to fifty decimal digits as 0.0020612874779541296.

Caveat — this corollary is not a statement about physical {}^3\mathrm{H} vs.\ {}^3\mathrm{He}. Under the canonical \bowtie_K-coupled convention the canonical formalism, {}^3\mathrm{H} has interface types (pn{=}\bowtie_K,\;nn{=}\sigma^{-1}) while {}^3\mathrm{He} has (pp{=}\sigma,\;pn{=}\bowtie_K) — the words differ in interface type, not just generator signs, so the sign-flip proposition does not apply directly. The legacy disjoint-product witness used by term7_alpha5_crystal_derivation artificially erases this isospin asymmetry.
